slot.brief: Ratio of de Broglie wavelengths of two particles (e.g. an alpha particle and a proton) accelerated through the same potential difference — numerical answer using λ ∝ 1/√(mq).

stem: An alpha particle and a proton are accelerated from rest through the same potential difference. Taking the mass of an alpha particle as four times that of a proton and its charge as twice that of a proton, the ratio of the de Broglie wavelength of the alpha particle to that of the proton is:

verdicts.working: For acceleration from rest, λ = h/√(2mqV). Thus λₐ/λₚ = √[(mₚe)/(4mₚ·2e)] = 1/(2√2).

working:
lambda = h / sqrt(2 m q V). Therefore lambda_alpha / lambda_p = sqrt(m_p q_p / (m_alpha q_alpha)) = sqrt(1 / (4 * 2)) = sqrt(1/8) = 1/(2 sqrt(2)).

Independent check: For acceleration from rest, λ = h/√(2mqV). Thus λₐ/λₚ = √[(mₚe)/(4mₚ·2e)] = 1/(2√2).
solution:
For a particle accelerated from rest through potential difference $V$, $4\lambda=\dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2mqV}}$.
$$\frac{\lambda_\alpha}{\lambda_p}=\sqrt{\frac{m_pq_p}{m_\alpha q_\alpha}}=\sqrt{\frac{1}{4\times2}}=\frac{1}{2\sqrt2}$$
